rules.title: any escapes type safety
rules.description: Explicit any, as-any cast, or implicit any at a boundary — pushes type errors to runtime. Suggest the precise type or unknown + narrowing.

rules.title: Non-null assertion masks a check
rules.description: The ! operator asserting away nullability where the value can actually be null/undefined on a reachable path.

rules.title: Floating promise
rules.description: A promise created without await, return, or .catch — rejections become unhandled and ordering is lost.

rules.title: Loose equality
rules.description: == / != with coercion where === was intended (null/undefined checks excepted if deliberate).

rules.title: Unhandled rejection path
rules.description: async function or promise chain with no error handling at the boundary — failures surface as unhandled rejections.

rules.title: Direct state/props mutation
rules.description: Mutating props, store state, or shared objects in place where immutability is expected (React/Redux/NgRx patterns).

rules.title: Type assertion hides a mismatch
rules.description: An as-cast (including as unknown as T) or satisfies-bypass that silences the compiler on data whose shape is not actually guaranteed: parsed JSON, request bodies, third-party values, narrowing from a wider type. Show what is being asserted and why it can be wrong. Prefer a type guard or schema validation. Do not record assertions on values just validated, DOM element lookups that are checked, or const assertions.

rules.title: External data used without validation
rules.description: Data from outside the process (JSON.parse results, HTTP request bodies or query strings, environment variables, files, message queues, API responses) used as typed values without runtime validation (schema library, type guard, explicit checks). Name the source and the first place the unvalidated value is relied on. Do not record when a validator runs earlier on the same path.

rules.title: Sequential await in a loop over independent work
rules.description: await inside a for/while loop where the iterations are independent, so latency adds up. Use Promise.all (bounded concurrency for large sets) or batch the calls. Do not record when order or rate limits require sequential execution, or when each iteration depends on the previous result.
